function.name: search_events
function.description: Search the event ledger by text, type, entity, status and date range. The primary way to answer questions about what happened.

query.description: Free text matched against titles, descriptions and event data.

entity_name.description: Restrict to events linked to this merchant/person/place.

date_range.description: today, yesterday, this week, last week, this month, last month, this year, "last N days", a single YYYY-MM-DD, or an explicit span "YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD".

function.name: get_event
function.description: One event in full: structured fields, every source it came from, related entities and events, and its edit history.

function.name: create_event
function.description: Record something that happened — a purchase, a booking, a milestone, a note. Use natural_language for a phrase like "petrol 1600 yesterday", or pass structured fields directly. NOT for meals, body measurements or workouts: use log_meal, log_measurement and log_activity for those — they store the shapes the Food screen and the charts read.

data.description: Facts: merchant, amount, currency, place, order_id…

allow_merge.description: False forces a separate event even if a similar one exists.

function.name: update_event
function.description: Correct an event. A correction from a person overwrites extracted values; the previous values are kept in the audit log.

changes.description: Any of occurred_at, type, subtype, title, description, data, inference, status, confidence.

replace_data.description: True replaces data wholesale instead of merging.

function.name: delete_or_dismiss_event
function.description: Dismiss an event that did not happen (reversible, keeps provenance, stops re-creation), or delete it outright with hard=true.

purge_sources.description: With hard=true, also remove source rows nothing else references.

function.name: log_meal
function.description: Record a meal: what was eaten, where and when. Use natural_language for a phrase like "2 packets maggi with 3 cheese slices", "had 2 idlis and a vada at Veena Stores at 7:30am" or "going to Ravi's place for dinner" — the last of which is a plan, and is stored as `scheduled` with no dishes until there are dishes to add. Dish names are snapped to the spellings already in the ledger, so "maggi" joins the Maggi you have eaten before instead of starting a second one. A meal carries no amount unless one is stated: eating is not buying, and the grocery order that paid for it is its own event. When the user states calories ("the Mac is 833"), pass them as kcal on the item — they are used verbatim, and remembered so that dish never needs estimating again.

occurred_at.description: ISO 8601. Overrides whatever the sentence implied.

place.description: Restaurant, shop or "Ravi's place". Omit for home.

items.description: What was eaten. Overrides the dishes read from the sentence.

amount.description: Per-item price, when the receipt stated one.

kcal.description: Calories for ONE of this item, when the user or the menu stated them. Used verbatim, never re-estimated.

kcal_estimated.description: Set true when the kcal is YOUR estimate rather than something the user or a menu stated. An estimate is remembered at model rank, not as the user's word.

amount.description: What the meal cost, if it was paid for here.

status.description: Defaults to what the tense implies.

function.name: add_meal_items
function.description: Add dishes to a meal already in the ledger — the "I will tell you what I ate later" half of log_meal. Pass event_id, or a date_range and the nearest food event in it is used. Quantities of a dish already listed are added together rather than duplicated, and a meal that was only planned becomes confirmed, since knowing what was on the plate is evidence it happened.

date_range.description: Used when event_id is absent. Defaults to today. today, yesterday, this week, last week, this month, last month, this year, "last N days", a single YYYY-MM-DD, or an explicit span "YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD".

function.name: lookup_barcode
function.description: Resolve a packaged food from its barcode and remember it, so every future receipt naming that product is priced automatically. Use this when the user photographs or reads out a barcode. A barcode is an exact identifier, not a search, so the result comes from the product's printed label and is trusted accordingly — unlike a nutrition lookup by name, which is a guess. Set eaten true to also log it as a meal right now; otherwise the product is only added to the dictionary and nothing is recorded as consumed.

barcode.description: EAN or UPC, 8 to 14 digits. Spaces and dashes are ignored.

eaten.description: Also log this as eaten now. Default false — scanning a pack is not eating it.

qty.description: How many packs, when eaten is true. Default 1.

occurred_at.description: ISO 8601. Defaults to now, when eaten is true.

name.description: Override the product name from the label.

function.name: get_nutrition
function.description: What the user actually ate over a period, in calories and protein. Use for "how many calories did I have today", "am I eating enough protein this week", "how did last month compare". ALWAYS report the coverage alongside the number: this is built from receipts, so anything cooked at home or paid in cash is invisible, and a total over 60% of meals means something different from one over 95%. Averages are per day the user actually ate something priced, never per calendar day, because dividing by days with no receipt would invent a diet nobody has.

date_range.description: Defaults to today. today, yesterday, this week, last week, this month, last month, this year, "last N days", a single YYYY-MM-DD, or an explicit span "YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD".

by.description: Break the period down. Default total.

function.name: set_food_nutrition
function.description: Record or correct the nutrition of one dish, from a label the user read out or a number they know. Values are per ONE SERVING AS SOLD — one thali, one packet, one whole pizza — not per 100g; convert before calling, using portion_g to say what mass that serving is. This marks the dish verified, which outranks every automatic estimate permanently and applies retroactively to every meal that ever contained it. Use it when the user disputes a number.

name.description: The dish, spelled as it appears on receipts.

portion_g.description: Mass of one serving in grams. Strongly preferred — it is what makes the number checkable.

function.name: list_unresolved_foods
function.description: Dishes the ledger has seen but has no nutrition for, most-eaten first. Use this to find out what is dragging coverage down, or to ask the user about the handful of dishes that would improve the numbers most. Resolving these is what makes get_nutrition trustworthy.

function.name: log_measurement
function.description: Record a body measurement — weight, waist, body fat. Use when the user states a reading: "88.4 this morning", "waist is 96cm". One reading per metric per day: telling it again the same day corrects the earlier value instead of duplicating it, so the user can re-weigh freely. Weight is the one that matters most here — it is the feedback loop for the daily calorie target — so when the user mentions weight in passing, offer to log it.

value.description: The reading, in the unit below.

unit.description: Defaults: weight kg, waist/chest cm, body_fat %, resting_hr bpm.

occurred_at.description: ISO 8601. Defaults to now. The reading belongs to its local day.

function.name: log_activity
function.description: Record exercise or physical activity: a workout, a run, a walk, a sport. Use when the user says they did something physical — "went to the gym", "ran 5k", "played badminton for an hour". Facts the user stated (what, how long, how far) land as facts; any estimated calorie burn is stored as inference, clearly separated, because the user said what they did, not what it burned.

activity.description: What they did: gym, run, walk, cycling, swimming, badminton, yoga…

intensity.description: Only if the user characterised it.

est_kcal_burned.description: Your estimate, if the user asks for one. Stored as inference, never as fact.

function.name: get_daily_summary
function.description: The stored summary for one day, with a live event count so a stale summary is visible as stale.

function.name: get_period_summary
function.description: A week or month: the stored retrospective if one exists, plus live aggregates and the daily summaries inside it.

function.name: get_entity
function.description: One merchant, person, place or project: how often it appears, when it was first and last seen, and the total spent with it.

function.name: search_entity_events
function.description: Every event linked to an entity. "What have I bought from Amazon", "when was I last in Hyderabad", "meetings with this person".

date_range.description: today, yesterday, this week, last week, this month, last month, this year, "last N days", a single YYYY-MM-DD, or an explicit span "YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD".

function.name: search_entities
function.description: Find entities by name. Use this to turn "Amazon" into an entity_id before calling search_entity_events.

function.name: get_stats
function.description: Aggregates over a period: counts by type, spend by category, top entities, how much needs review. Computed from events at call time, never stored.

date_range.description: today, yesterday, this week, last week, this month, last month, this year, "last N days", a single YYYY-MM-DD, or an explicit span "YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD".

function.name: get_review_queue
function.description: Events the system is unsure about, for confirming, correcting, merging or dismissing.

function.name: merge_events
function.description: Fold a duplicate into a target event. All evidence moves across; the target keeps its facts.

function.name: export_ledger
function.description: Everything, as JSON: events with their sources, entities and summaries. The data is yours and portable.

date_range.description: today, yesterday, this week, last week, this month, last month, this year, "last N days", a single YYYY-MM-DD, or an explicit span "YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD".
